grid-tilesize-overlap-2026-08-18: Post-hoc (E41-class) 2x2 tile-size x overlap grid, proposer stage only, consensus-only aggregation, 10 passes per cell, one configuration throughout (detect_brief-text, gemini-3-flash-preview, MINIMAL, T=0.7; 30,130 calls, $18.53 billed). Scored on the four-way tile-union intersection carried on the era-2-487 grid (487 carrier tiles, 20 m buffer), with the preregistered 20 m within-pass deduplication applied to every pass so denser tilings are not penalised for cross-tile duplicates. Best cell per configuration at K=10: 512 px / 12.5 % F1 0.6845 [0.6336,0.7313] MCC 0.5431; 512 px / 50 % F1 0.7611 [0.7126,0.8023] MCC 0.5853; 384 px / 12.5 % F1 0.6574 [0.6038,0.7056] MCC 0.3066; 384 px / 50 % F1 0.7293 [0.6841,0.7686] MCC 0.4909. TWO STANDING PRIORS OVERTURNED. (1) 512 px wins at every overlap and every K, so the 384 px sweet spot does NOT reproduce under one footprint at T=0.7: tile-size effect -0.0803 at 12.5 % [-0.1236,-0.0394] and -0.0976 at 50 % [-0.1206,-0.0752], both excluding zero. (2) Passes do NOT substitute for overlap: 384 px / 12.5 % at K=10 loses to 512 px / 50 % at K=3 by 0.0304 union recall and 0.0926 best F1, at lower cost. NOTE THE SIGN ON OVERLAP: the paired contrasts are computed on run-averaged single-pass per-tile counts with NO consensus filter, so (12.5 % - 50 %) = +0.1207 at 512 px and +0.1381 at 384 px means 50 % overlap COSTS about 0.12-0.14 F1 at a single pass. Overlap reverses and becomes the most valuable factor in the grid only once the corroboration filter it creates is switched on -- which is why the best cell is a 50 % one. Tile size never reverses. The interaction is UNRESOLVED: difference-of-differences -0.0173 [-0.0580,+0.0248], p=0.4033, spanning zero. ALL OF THIS IS CONDITIONAL ON THE ABSENCE OF A PRECISION STAGE: no verifier has run over any grid cell, so whether the tile-size ranking and the overlap effect survive verification is untested (recall-levers programme Phase 1, $6.33). Bootstrap intervals here are at B=10,000 per the 2026-08-19 PI ruling (erratum E82), not the 1,000 Decision 10 pre-specified; the paired contrasts use the analysis script's own resampler, which was never on the D15 defective path, so re-running them at 10,000 moved every delta by 0.00000, every CI width by under 5 %, and no significance verdict. Two of 228 swept cells have an undefined tile MCC, reported as null and never as 0.0 (E81). Artefacts: results/grid-2026-08-18/{grid_analysis.json,sweep.csv,findings.md} and the four per-cell evaluations under results/grid-2026-08-18/conditions/; scripts grid_prepare_scoring.py, grid_analysis.py, grid_materialise_conditions.py.
grid-postverifier-2026-08-18: Post-hoc (E41-class) proposer-verifier board for the tile-size x overlap grid: the four committed K=10 unions (c>=1, k>=1; 1,402/2,585/1,827/3,319 candidates, documented counts reproduced EXACTLY at materialisation) verified by the study's carry-forward adversarial text verifier (gemini-3-flash-preview, T=0.0, MINIMAL, n=1; 9,133/9,133 verified, ZERO failures; metas $12.5428 list -> $6.2714 expected flex billed vs $6.33 costed, -$0.06), then thresholded on (mound_probability, vote_count) and scored for $0 with the grid's own machinery on the common 487-tile footprint at 20 m (580-row prob_t x k sweep). Best per cell (best-F1@20m; BCa CI95 at B=10,000): 384/50 p>=0.15 k>=10 F1 0.9017 [0.8727,0.9244] MCC 0.8037; 512/50 p>=0.15 k>=9 F1 0.8870 [0.8583,0.9118] MCC 0.8087; 384/12.5 p>=0.15 k>=7 F1 0.8761 MCC 0.7852 (the registered condition keeps p>=0.20 k>=7: F1 0.8752 [0.8424,0.9017] MCC 0.7852); 512/12.5 p>=0.15 k>=5 F1 0.8368 [0.7995,0.8676] MCC 0.8011. BOTH QUESTIONS THE CONSENSUS-ONLY BOARD LEFT OPEN ARE SETTLED, THE SECOND AT 512 PX ONLY. (1) The tile-size ranking REVERSES under the full pipeline: (384-512) = +0.0393 [+0.0052,+0.0741] p=0.0266 at 12.5% overlap — excluding zero on the OPPOSITE side of the consensus-only -0.0803 — and +0.0147 [-0.0095,+0.0394] p=0.2454 at 50% (sign reversed, unresolved). The consensus-only '512 px challenge' to the study's 384 px preference was a truncated-pipeline artefact: the verifier recovers the precision 384 px lacked, while the 384 px cells' higher union-recall ceilings (0.9112/0.9696 vs 0.8879/0.9603) are the resource a verifier cannot create — the Obs 352 rescue mechanism at a new tile-size pair. (2) The overlap reversal SURVIVES the verifier at 512 px but FAILS at 384 px: 50% wins significantly at 512 px ((12.5-50) = -0.0502 [-0.0778,-0.0224] p=0.0003) but not at 384 px (-0.0256 [-0.0517,+0.0001] p=0.0541, the interval reaching +0.0001), at roughly HALF the consensus-only margin — the corroboration filter and the verifier are partially redundant, and the surviving advantage tracks the recall-ceiling edge, as the findings doc predicted. Interaction unresolved (-0.0246 [-0.0613,+0.0114], p=0.1831). CONSENSUS AND VERIFIER ARE COMPLEMENTS, NOT SUBSTITUTES: every cell's best operating point retains a vote threshold (k>=5..10) atop the probability threshold; the pure-verifier k=1 board tops out at 0.8187 (384/12.5) and trails the stacked optimum in every cell by 0.057-0.207. The 384 px tile-MCC saturation pathology dissolves post-verifier (all four cells MCC 0.785-0.809; F1 and MCC rankings broadly agree). Verifier gain over the consensus-only board +0.126..+0.219 best-F1, largest where consensus-only was worst (the 384 px cells). GATES, all passed: exact union-count reproduction at materialisation (stop rule); contiguous candidate-key join; carrier-tile reassignment after the CRS round-trip; each unthresholded union re-scores to its committed sweep row (<=1e-6); each materialised condition reproduces its sweep F1 to <=5e-5 at B=10,000. The paired tile-bootstrap contrasts are the significance instrument (Decision 10 resampler, B=10,000 per E82, seed 42, integer per-tile counts of each single verified set); per-cell CIs are register metadata. Best-F1 operating points are selected on the same ground truth they are scored on, as on the consensus board (E41-class calibration caveat). Artefacts: results/grid-2026-08-18/{verifier_analysis.json,verifier_sweep.csv} and findings.md section 'The verifier stage, run'; the four evaluations under results/grid-2026-08-18/conditions-verified/; verifier inputs and raw outputs under outputs/grid-2026-08-18/verifier/ (committed 8eda1e3a3); scripts materialise_grid_unions.py, grid_verifier_analysis.py. [REVISED 2026-08-24, same-day audit (commits 57b7ad7ad/0a6bde47f): the pre/post tile-size framing above cites the single-pass contrasts (-0.0824/-0.0972, both significant), which run-average ten passes and are not the like-for-like baseline for a single aggregated operating point. The proper pre-verifier arm — the registered K=10 best consensus-only operating points on the same instrument, now published as bootstrap_contrasts_consensus_k10_baseline — gives (384-512) = -0.0284 [-0.0813,+0.0233] p=0.281 at 12.5% and -0.0312 [-0.0695,+0.0052] p=0.089 at 50%: BOTH NON-SIGNIFICANT. The correct statement of the reversal is therefore: aggregation alone erodes 512px's significant single-pass advantage to non-significance, and the verifier then flips the sign, significantly at 12.5% (+0.0366 p=0.034). The overlap baseline is -0.0758 p=0.0004 / -0.0730 p=0.0026, so the overlap conclusion is unchanged. Every board value, post-verifier contrast, and registered condition is unchanged by the audit; the join was additionally verified at source over all 9,133 candidates against the now-committed candidate manifests (ids contiguous in feature order, centroids within 0.069 m against 5.6-8.0 m minimum spacing). Selection-space caveat added to the findings doc: operating points are F1-selected on the scored tiles, and the post-verifier sweep offers ~4-5x the consensus sweep's selection space.]

gemini37-screen-2026-08-28: G1's pre-named informative outcome FIRED and G2 is falsified. The carried-verifier K=5 cell reaches 0.9238 @20 m at (0.10, k5) on a 791-candidate union, nominally above every Gemini-3 cell on this corpus, but the paired tile-swap permutation (10,000 draws, 487 tiles) returns +0.0221 at p = 0.0971 against a null SD of 0.0134 — below the GS instrument's resolution, so the screen can name the direction and not the size. K=10 adds +0.0006 (0.9243, p = 0.1231) and the ladder's own N5-N10 contrast is -0.0013 at p = 0.7921: saturated by N = 5, the Gemini-3 shape exactly (0.8652 / 0.9118 / 0.9231 / 0.9243 at N = 1/3/5/10). The headline is the role swap: re-verifying the SAME 791 candidates with gemini-3.7-flash reaches 0.9364 @20 m at (0.80, k5), P 0.9268 / R 0.9463 / tile-MCC 0.8192 — +0.0347 vs the anchor, p = 0.0065, the study's first GS-resolvable model-swap margin and the only cell in the arc beating the anchor on F1 and MCC together. The mechanism is calibration, not judgement: the 3.7 verifier's mean mound_probability is 0.699 against the carried verifier's 0.594 on identical candidates (0.687 / 0.587 before the re-verified rows, planning/gemini37-screen-2026-08-28.md:110), so its optimum migrates four rungs up a lattice that has sat at 0.10-0.20 across every model the study has run — G2 falsified, and the portable claim is that a verifier's operating threshold does not transfer across verifier models. Cost ordering is the practitioner lesson: five extra passes cost ~$5.4 and bought +0.0006; the role swap cost ~$0.9 token-basis and bought +0.0126 over the same union. Caveats: both sides of every contrast are sweep-selected argmaxes scored on the same reference; this is a single comparison with no family correction across four GS sheets; and 3.7-`low` emits ~276 thinking tokens per tile against Gemini-3 MINIMAL's zero, so model and thinking stay confounded. The K=10 escalation re-verified the full union rather than increment-stitching — disclosed on the card, cheaper than the matching-error risk, and it gives single-vintage probabilities. The ladder rungs are re-derived; registration pending materialisation. Obs 441.
gemini37-image-gs-2026-09-01: The modality gap is eliminated at Gemini 3.7. A difference-in-differences on one geometry and one reference: (text - image) within Gemini 3 was +0.0559 at p = 0.0005; within 3.7 it is -0.0143 (p = 0.158) on the carried-verifier pair and -0.0043 (p = 0.6767) on the all-3.7 pair — a gap change of -0.060 to -0.070, roughly 2.5x the GS verified-set resolution (MDE80 ~ 0.025), so a resolved change and not instrument noise. The honest claim is PARITY, not inversion: image leads nominally in both pairs and neither sign flip is close to significant. I2 predicted the gap would land below ~0.031 and the outcome overshot to zero. I1 is confirmed at about four times the text-side family gain — 3.7-image reaches 0.9381 (carried verifier, at (0.05, k5); 0.9353 at its registered (0.10, k5)) and 0.9408 (3.7 verifier) against the 0.8458 Gemini-3 image anchor, gains of +0.0923 / +0.0950 where the same family step on text was +0.022 — so the gap closed because image caught up, not because text regressed, and the 3-to-3.7 step delivers most of its value where pixels are read. I3 FAILS on the carried-verifier arm, whose optimum moved to (0.05, k5), below the predicted 0.10-0.20, and is confirmed on the 3.7-verifier arm at (0.90, k5): the 3.7 verifier's high-probability calibration shift replicates on image candidates, a second instrument for the non-transferring-threshold claim. I4 is confirmed and lighter than predicted (88-157 t/call). I5 is an informative failure — implicit caching engaged at 79.5 % of input against a registered >= 90 % bar, with the probe warm-up-confounded (16 % cold-parallel, 54 % sequential), yet the proposer side cost $22.50 token-basis against a $32-36 projection. The escalation trigger is NOT met: all-3.7 image 0.9408 against the all-3.7 text swap 0.9364 is +0.0043 at p = 0.677, far inside MDE80, no resolvable new high, so the 55-map image extension does not proceed — a registered negative decision, not an absence. Obliges the paper: the study's 'text examples beat image examples' claim must be reframed as Gemini-3-specific. Obs 447.

gemini38-screen-armv-2026-09-04: The family ladder stops at 3.7. On the identical 791-candidate union, the 3.8 verifier reaches 0.9358 @20 m at (0.88, k5), P 0.9347 / R 0.9369 / tile-MCC 0.8331 on 429 detections: against the all-3.7 stack that is dF1 -0.0006 at p = 0.7769, and against the carried Gemini-3 verifier +0.0120 at p = 0.0764. E1 CONFIRMED — a tie, and the pre-named informative outcome did not fire, so the verifier-model policy stays shut and the 55-map board is untouched. The tie is not flat on every axis: 3.8 buys +0.0139 of tile-MCC over 3.7 (0.8331 vs 0.8192) while losing 0.0006 of F1, precision-led as its point implies. E3 is FALSIFIED in the opposite direction — 76 thinking tokens per candidate in the verifier seat against the 3.7 verifier's 106, and only 1.1x in the proposer probe (307 vs 275 t/tile), so 'newer' bought LESS thinking, not more. E4 is only partly confirmed, and the check that settles it also corrects the campaign's first reading: the argmax does sit at 0.88 rather than at 3.7's 0.80/0.85 or Gemini-3's 0.15/0.20, but the surface is flat — every k=5 point from prob_t 0.20 to 0.92 lies within 0.0022 of the best — AND the 3.7 verifier is equally flat on the same union (0.9343-0.9364 over that band, spread 0.0022, swap37/sweep_20m.csv), whereas the carried Gemini-3 verifier is sharply peaked (0.8520-0.9021, spread 0.0502). Threshold insensitivity is therefore a 3.7/3.8-generation property, not a 3.8 novelty. E2 is untested: the PI ruled STOP after Arm V, so Arm P (~$9.6) and Arm S (~$1) were not run; total spend was ~$0.85 flex token-basis. Gotchas recorded on the card: run_pv.py verify stamps cost_basis 'list' with discount 1.0 even under --service-tier flex; the verify path counts each retried server error as a parse failure (803 = retries_total); and cleanup overwrote run.meta.json again, the main-run meta surviving as run.meta.main-2026-09-04.json.
